reuse.why: Most month-wide actions share getBulkEditableCategories and reuse existing budget, sheet, batching, and undo helpers, but copyPreviousMonth implements eligibility separately.

duplication.why: The selector removes repeated category queries, but eligibility remains duplicated between SQL and copyPreviousMonth, and the new action repeats the income eligibility guard.

placement.why: Budget selection and calculations remain in budget/actions.ts, with method registration and undo wrapping in budget/app.ts.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested month-wide rules, new action, registration, supporting test, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared selector improves ownership, but future eligibility changes still require coordinated updates to its SQL and copyPreviousMonth's separate predicate.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth bypasses getBulkEditableCategories and independently applies hidden, saved-template, and fixed-group exclusions.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: getBulkEditableCategories expresses hidden and saved-template eligibility in SQL and fixed-group eligibility in a filter, while copyPreviousMonth reshapes the same policy into a JavaScript conditional using hasSavedTemplates.

abstraction_drift.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: getBulkEditableCategories gains includeHiddenCategories and a conditional SQL fragment for hidden filtering, while copyPreviousMonth maintains a parallel eligibility implementation.
